answers.answer: Each player takes twelve ordinary turns: the 16 spaces contain four seasons of three ordinary rounds plus a courtship. Courtship is an event with no player turns, service rotation, monument income, or Servants’ Hall use.
answers.evidence: Overview: ‘each player takes twelve ordinary turns’; courtship is an event with ‘no player turns, service rotation, monument income or Servants’ Hall use.’

answers.answer: Hosting order: (1) rotate service, moving servants in Servants’ Quarters to Available Service, then Expended Service to Servants’ Quarters; (2) resolve the round-track event, then applicable monument and Servants’ Hall effects in either order; (3) choose an activity tile; (4) invite the exact required number and types of gentry; (5) staff every required service icon; (6) collect favours, resolving all positive before negative; (7) optionally buy one improvement; (8) send every used servant to Expended Service, played gentry to the personal discard pile, and return the tile to its tableau column, flipping/upgrading as required. The last player advances the round marker.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure → Hosting an activity, steps 1–8.

answers.answer: Passing order: all servants directly to Available Service; all gentry in your discard to hand; resolve the round-track event, then ongoing tile effects; choose £200 or a free Market refresh; optionally buy one tile; then the last player advances the marker. Servants used for an ongoing effect during the pass are expended at turn end. Butler’s Room hiring is an activity, not a passing benefit, so you cannot hire through it while passing.
answers.evidence: Passing: ‘all servants directly to Available Service → all gentry in your discard to hand → round-track event, then ongoing tile effects → choose £200 or a free Market refresh → optional one tile purchase’; hiring is ‘an activity in this base scope, not a passing benefit.’

answers.answer: Yes. It is legal to play the PR6 activity and PR6 guests: screening uses the reputation level at the end of step 2, before Choose Activity, so 6.1 qualifies. Later Service Help actions may lower actual reputation to 3.4 without invalidating the activity. Service Help moves one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service; it cannot take one directly from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Reputation screening is fixed at the end of step 2 and remains the screening level for the whole activity; Service Help moves a servant ‘from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service’ and cannot take one directly from Expended Service.

answers.answer: Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours; within each group their order is your choice. At minimum reputation, a negative reputation favour cannot be taken first to avoid the loss: negative reputation cannot go below 1.1. A money penalty must be fully payable. You may use positive money favours from the activity, a money VP card, or Borrow Money; if short, you must borrow if possible, and if you still cannot fund it, you cannot play that guest or tile.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 6 requires ‘all positive favours before all negative favours’; money penalty rule says it must be fully payable and, if short, ‘you must borrow if possible.’ Special Rules: negative reputation cannot take reputation below 1.1.

answers.answer: Borrow Money costs 2 reputation increments and gains £100; it is repeatable. Service Help costs 3 increments and moves one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service; it is repeatable. Refresh Market costs 4 increments and fully refreshes the Market; that special action is limited to once per turn. At minimum reputation (1.1), you cannot take a special action. Service Help cannot take a servant directly from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Special actions table lists each cost/effect and limit; reputation section says at minimum ‘you cannot … take a special action’; Service Help cannot take a servant directly from Expended Service.

answers.answer: Use Butler’s Room as a Servant Hiring activity with an available butler or underbutler and no gentry. Take up to two servants from Servants for Hire, excluding underbutlers, into Expended Service; there is no hiring fee. On its upgraded side, instead of hiring up to two from supply, recruit one common servant (footman, valet, or lady’s maid) from any location on one opponent’s family board into your Expended Service. Unique servants cannot be recruited.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring → Butler’s Room: ‘no gentry’; up to two from supply into Expended Service; upgraded room recruits one common servant from ‘any location on one opponent’s family board.’

answers.answer: A housekeeper may substitute for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. With a Brushing Room in your tableau, a footman may substitute for a valet only when no valets are available. An underbutler may substitute for any base male servant (butler, valet, footman) even when that servant type remains available.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: substitution rules for housekeeper, footman with Brushing Room, and underbutler.

answers.answer: The only way to acquire an underbutler is to purchase Butler’s Pantry; take one from supply immediately into Expended Service. It is not immediately available: normally it moves to Servants’ Quarters at your next service rotation and to Available Service at your second subsequent rotation. Passing or a Refresh Service VP card can make it available earlier; once it is in Quarters, Service Help or the Servants’ Quarters tile can permit earlier use. Another player cannot recruit it: the upgraded Butler’s Room recruits only common servants, and underbutlers cannot be hired through Butler’s Room or Hire Servant VP cards.
answers.evidence: Butler’s Pantry paragraph gives acquisition, Expended Service destination and rotation timing; Butler’s Room paragraph limits recruiting to common servants; Hire Servant VP cards exclude underbutlers.

answers.answer: Market price is the market-space price plus the tile’s printed price modifier. Reserve price is £300 plus the modifier. A tile cannot cost less than £100. You may not acquire a duplicate tile you already own by any means. Reputation does not restrict purchasing, so a tile above your reputation may be bought.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve: ‘market-space price plus the tile’s printed price modifier’; Reserve base price £300; minimum £100; never acquire a duplicate; reputation does not restrict purchasing.

answers.answer: When a Market space becomes empty, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into the rightmost spaces. Stack a drawn duplicate on its matching tile already in the Market and draw again. A Reserve-eligible tile goes straight to Reserve, then draw again. If filling multiple spaces, sort only the new tiles by ascending sorting number. Buying one tile from a two-tile stack leaves that space occupied, so it does not trigger a refill.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve → Refill specifies sliding, duplicate stacking, Reserve routing, sorting new tiles, and that buying one from a two-tile stack leaves an occupied space.

answers.answer: After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles except Largest Wine Cellar to Reserve; later Service tiles drawn go directly there, with the same exception. After courtship 2, also move all Market PR1 tiles to Reserve; later PR1 draws go directly there. Largest Wine Cellar never enters Reserve. A full Market refresh after each of the first three courtships is standard in this rules scope.
answers.evidence: Open Reserve: after courtship 1 Service tiles move except Largest Wine Cellar and future Service draws go there; after courtship 2 PR1 tiles move and future PR1 draws go there. Refresh: full refresh after each of the first three courtships; standard scope confirms it is required.

answers.answer: At each courtship, first return both Fairchilds to Alderley Hall, wherever held. In courtships 1–3, score the current face-up theme’s tile VP, including negative values; only the currently face-up hybrid category counts. The highest scorer draws one VP card and chooses one Fairchild for their hand. If tied for highest, each tied player draws one VP card and no one gets a Fairchild. Every player discards one secret objective; shuffle simultaneous discards together and put them on the bottom of the deck. After courtships 1–3, pass the first-player marker anticlockwise.
answers.evidence: Courtship and seasonal upkeep gives the return order, theme scoring, winner and tie outcomes, objective discard, and seasonal order including passing first-player marker anticlockwise.

answers.answer: At final courtship, return Fairchilds as usual and score tile VP for all four revealed theme cards; repeated categories count each time, including negative VP. Highest score gets one VP card and a Fairchild. On a tie, highest reputation level breaks it, with wheel position ignored; if still tied, no Fairchild is awarded and tied winners draw VP cards under the courtship tie rule. Discard the final objective. Then players may take a final chance to use special actions and VP cards for their benefits where possible before the marker moves to Wedding Bells and scoring.
answers.evidence: Final courtship paragraph specifies all-four-theme scoring, ties, final objective discard, and final opportunity to use special actions and VP cards.

answers.answer: End-game VP categories are improvement tiles (printed face-up VP, including negatives), gentry in hand and discard (including negatives, family, and final Fairchild; dismissed guests excluded), fulfilled objectives, reputation, servants, wealth, and retained unused VP cards. Reputation levels 1–7 score respectively 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, and 28 VP. Wealth scores 1 VP per £200, rounded down. Victory ties go first to the tied player with the final Fairchild; otherwise the tied player with the highest reputation level wins; if still tied, victory is shared. Reputation wheel position does not break the tie.
answers.evidence: Final VP table lists each source, the reputation sequence and £200 rounded-down wealth scoring; victory paragraph gives Fairchild, reputation-level, then shared-victory tiebreaks.

answers.answer: Normally each player gets five secret objectives at setup and draws two more on round 6. Discard one at each of the four courtships, leaving three to score. Shuffle simultaneous discards together, then put them face down on the bottom of the objective deck. A tile objective requires owning the named tile at game end; it does not need to be upgraded.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards: five at setup plus two on round 6; discard one at each of four courtships, leaving three; simultaneous discards are shuffled together; tile objectives require owning tiles, not upgrading them.

answers.answer: A VP card’s benefit may be used immediately when drawn, at any time on your later turn (multiple cards may be used), and once more after final courtship before scoring. Used VP cards go to the bottom of the VP deck. Retained, unused cards stay hidden with objectives and score their printed VP at game end; a card cannot provide both its benefit and final VP.
answers.evidence: VP card rules state when benefits can be used, that used cards go to the bottom of the VP deck, and retained cards stay hidden with objectives; you cannot take both benefit and final VP.

answers.answer: A normal activity tile must flip to its rose/upgrade side after its first use; once upgraded, it stays on that side on later uses. A hybrid starts with its underlined icon showing, flips after every use, and moves to the newly face-up category. A tile that upgrades into an ongoing monument (Queen’s Suite or Lionheart Suite) has one activity use, then becomes a monument and can never host again; its monument benefit starts on subsequent turns. For a hybrid, only its currently face-up category counts at courtship and for objectives.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects gives normal and hybrid flip rules and says only the face-up category counts for courtship and objectives; Monuments and suite entries describe suite upgrade into monument and later benefit.

answers.answer: Monuments resolve during the ongoing-effects step on ordinary turns, whether hosting or passing; each gives one reputation. There is no monument income during courtship. Servants’ Hall also resolves during the ongoing-effects step (step 2 when hosting, step 3 when passing): place one available servant on it to reduce one opponent’s reputation by one and gain one reputation yourself. That servant cannot also staff the activity and goes to Expended Service at turn end. You may not target a player at minimum reputation.
answers.evidence: Monuments: one reputation per ordinary turn during ongoing effects, hosting or passing, no courtship income. Servants’ Hall specifies its timing, one available servant, reputation changes, expending, and minimum-reputation targeting restriction.

answers.answer: Heritage Guest Suite uses one casual guest from hand and a footman on the tile; provide the guest’s normal service. It doubles all guest favours, including negative ones, then upgrades and remains an activity tile. Queen’s Suite uses one prestige guest from hand and a housekeeper on the tile; provide normal guest service. It doubles one chosen favour and resolves the others normally, then upgrades into a monument. Lionheart Suite draws one prestige guest from the deck to attend, uses a butler on the tile, and requires no personal guest service. It doubles nonnegative favours while negative favours are excluded from doubling; keep the drawn guest and put it in your discard at cleanup, then the tile upgrades into a monument. Each suite has a fixed count of one guest that cannot be increased or decreased.
answers.evidence: Suite activity table lists each guest source/type, tile service, guest service, favour doubling, cleanup and later tile state; following paragraph says all three have a fixed count of one guest.
